IN ACTIVE DEVELOPMENT

Weather Alerts

A live severe-weather overlay system — pulling NWS alerts straight onto the living room TV, so the alert shows up on screen the moment it's issued, without touching a remote.

Alert sourceNWS API, polled every 60s
Display targetGoogle TV device
DeliveryCast overlay, no input switch needed
01

How it works

NWS API

Polled every minute — either through Home Assistant's nws_alerts integration or a custom poller — for active alerts covering the area.

↓

TV overlay

Pushed to the living room's Google TV box through the TvOverlay app, which draws the alert directly over whatever's on screen — no need to switch inputs or interrupt what's casting.

02

Two tiers of display

Corner badge

A lightweight, persistent alert badge for lower-severity events — title, severity color, and icon, pushed via TvOverlay's notify_fixed endpoint. Expires automatically when the alert does.

Full news-style overlay

For higher-severity alerts: an HTML layout with the affected area map, a radar loop, and a scrolling marquee — captured by a headless browser, encoded with FFmpeg into a live HLS stream, and pushed as video through TvOverlay.

03

Build status

BUILT

Lower-third ticker prototype

An HTML overlay at 1920×1080 with a transparent background for compositing — sunset-gradient logo badge, CSS-animated scrolling ticker, a self-updating clock, and a setWeather() hook ready to receive live NWS data.

IN PROGRESS

Persistent always-on overlay

Three approaches researched — a custom Android TV app using TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY, an inline HDMI compositor, and a dedicated companion screen. No decision made yet on which one ships.

PLANNED

Non-Android-TV fallback

For cast devices that aren't Android TV boxes, a Cast-takeover approach using Home Assistant's Lovelace cast or a registered custom Web Receiver.
